nodes.title: How much prefill fits in this iteration
nodes.behavior: The adder continues the unfinished request, then scans waiting requests. Compute budgets charge extend plus replay rows. Exhaustion can stop a pass while KV is still free.
conditions: AGG or PD prefill; normal PrefillAdder path.
confounders: DP divides declared chunk size; mixed decode consumes budget; page alignment; replay rows; max request limits; one unchunked request can exceed nominal input cap.
nodes.hypothesis: If token budget binds with queued work and spare KV, a larger batch may improve P capacity; it may increase TTFT/ITL and workspace demand.
nodes.next_test: At fixed per-rank request cap, raise only the effective token budget. Compare admitted extend/replay rows, P stage time, queue slope and live decode activity.
nodes.remaining_gap: Not all specialized DLLM/ignore-EOS stops have reason logs; inspect residual budget/queue evidence.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Admission reserves space for future output
nodes.behavior: The running-request future-growth estimate uses a changing ratio. Candidate admission and special paths have their own bounds; this is not a physical reservation of every predicted token.
conditions: Most relevant to AGG; P-only outputs and D preallocation use different accounting.
confounders: Attention DP scales configured conservativeness by 0.3 in parallel_hook; output limits; ignore_eos; retraction resets; cache locks.
nodes.hypothesis: Lower headroom may admit more work when output limits overpredict actual answers, but can cause retraction when outputs run long.
nodes.next_test: Hold output distribution constant; compare occupancy, retracted tokens, latency tails and memory-budget refusals.
nodes.remaining_gap: No claim that one ratio controls every admission path; logs report reservations rather than attributing all refusals to this knob.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Decode capacity before incoming transfer
nodes.behavior: D admits destination storage before publishing indices. It accounts for request rows, metadata rows, FULL/SWA constraints, active headroom and recoverability of in-flight work.
conditions: PD decode; regular device preallocation instrumentation.
confounders: Decode prefix hits and pending loadback; allocator shared-pool feasibility; max output; active/retracted requests; host receive changes path.
nodes.hypothesis: Extra slots help only if rows bind; they do not create KV capacity. Lower headroom may trade concurrency for retraction risk.
nodes.next_test: First separate handshake, slot and KV gates. If KV binds compare required/budget values and per-pool capacity; change one limit.
nodes.remaining_gap: KV failure can be joint physical capacity even if scalar FULL/SWA budgets look sufficient. Host allocation success and retransfers are not fully instrumented.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: When P runs and D reserves KV
nodes.behavior: Optimism permits P computation before destination indices. Deferred allocation waits for prefill readiness; notification does not guarantee capacity or transfer overlap.
conditions: PD; compare the resolved policy on both roles.
confounders: Network/bootstrap discovery; D memory pressure; poll cadence; current forward length; cancellation/retraction.
nodes.hypothesis: Deferring reservations may free D for ready requests under long prefills, but adds handoff latency when capacity is plentiful.
nodes.next_test: Use matched long/short prompt distributions at low and high concurrency. Compare active D, prealloc usage, handoff latency, retries and TTFT.
nodes.remaining_gap: Bootstrapping status combines discovery and readiness; do not label all handshake_pending as waiting for prefill completion. Existing latency histograms are completion-biased.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Actual device KV capacity
nodes.behavior: Resolved pool capacity depends on weights, cache layout, workspace, graph capture and static-memory budgeting; a declared fraction alone is not the result.
conditions: Model and allocator specific; compare equal checkpoints and quantization.
confounders: Explicit max_total_tokens cap; compression accounting; graph capture size; DSpark draft pools; locked prefix pages.
nodes.hypothesis: More actual available KV can improve concurrency/cache retention when memory binds; increasing fraction is useless if another cap binds.
nodes.next_test: Record startup capacities and graph/workspace memory; compare per-pool pressure and refusals before changing fraction.
nodes.remaining_gap: Reserved workspace overhead by backend is not fully exported; no GPU-memory polling added.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: FULL, SWA and state compete differently
nodes.behavior: Fixed pools and shared-byte allocators have different feasibility checks. SWA can limit a request or shrink its chunk even with FULL tokens available.
conditions: Only hybrid attention/state models and supported allocator variants.
confounders: Request rings; bounded replay retention; prefix eviction; shared-pool holes/compaction.
nodes.hypothesis: Rebalancing pools can resolve a one-pool bottleneck; unified memory changes the tradeoff rather than guaranteeing a win.
nodes.next_test: Compare simultaneous FULL/SWA/state headroom and failures; vary ratio only with matching allocator/replay settings.
nodes.remaining_gap: Joint shared-byte shortfall not expressible as one token count; logs deliberately do not invent a limiting pool.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Prefix reuse versus recomputation
nodes.behavior: Prefix matching reduces new work; the useful hit depends on device, host or storage location and required replay.
conditions: Cache producers and metrics differ by cache implementation; D cache opt-in separate.
confounders: Router affinity; warmup/returning turns; eviction; requests retracted/recomputed; replayed cached rows.
nodes.hypothesis: A high hit rate can coexist with slow prefill if hits require loadback or replay; nominal matched tokens are not all avoided GPU work.
nodes.next_test: Use device/host/storage hit token rates, actual extend/replay work and loadback cost on matched traces.
nodes.remaining_gap: Cache metrics alone cannot establish counterfactual recompute savings.

nodes.title: Per-rank budgets and DP cooperation
nodes.behavior: Parallelism resolves effective per-rank limits and collective work. Attention DP divides the prefill chunk; synchronized ranks can prevent local graph replay.
conditions: DP metrics need their producer/configuration; per-rank identity required.
confounders: Asymmetric P/D sizes; collective fabric; routing imbalance; effective request caps; PP microbatches.
Current main separates replica dp_size from attn_dp_size. Deprecated --dp-size N --enable-dp-attention resolves to attn_dp_size=N and dp_size=1; compare resolved settings, not old recipe spellings.
nodes.hypothesis: Scaling width can lower utilization if ranks wait or cannot form useful batches; larger declared batch is not necessarily larger per-rank work.
nodes.next_test: Record resolved sizes, plot per-rank work and waiting; compare at fixed total GPUs and distinguish P capacity from D service rate.
nodes.remaining_gap: No built-in cross-service ratio recommendation; deployment worker counts belong to launcher, not a single SGLang flag.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Graph actually used versus enabled
nodes.behavior: Graph replay requires eligible shape, context, features, backend and DP agreement. Requested enablement does not imply covered AgentX steps.
conditions: Actual dispatch counters at ModelRunner; local eligibility can also be checked during scheduling.
confounders: Warmup/capture vs serving; capture memory shrinks KV; mixed modes; replay tail; runner may execute some operations eagerly.
nodes.hypothesis: Wider capture coverage may remove CPU launch overhead but costs memory; benefit requires actual replay on the workload.
nodes.next_test: Verify constructed runner logs and dispatch after warmup, diagnose first eligibility failure; compare paired graph on/off with fixed capacities.
nodes.remaining_gap: Eligibility event counts can include schedule-time and forward-time checks; cannot divide them by forwards. Not all decode fallback reasons are instrumented. Dispatch is not proof every layer used a graph.

nodes.title: Cached rows still computed for bounded replay
nodes.behavior: Encoder replay contributes compute rows to admission; decoder replay and graph eligibility affect how repeated layers execute and how cache tails are retained.
conditions: DSv4.1-style supported model paths.
confounders: Graph coverage; SWA capacity; cache hits; MegaMoE max-token workspace; draft stages.
nodes.hypothesis: Replay can free KV capacity yet introduce CPU or GPU work; its net gain depends on capacity pressure and execution path.
nodes.next_test: Compare admitted replay rows and capacities alongside actual graph use and forward timing; separate tail-only vs full-prefill graph experiments.
nodes.remaining_gap: Per-layer eager replay tail CPU/GPU split still requires profiler; row counts alone do not measure cost.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Backend selection and workspace
nodes.behavior: MoE runner and A2A choices interact with model, weights, dtype, workspace and library version. The selected wrapper does not prove the library internal kernel variant.
conditions: Supported hardware, model and installed FlashInfer/DeepGEMM APIs.
confounders: CUDA graph replay bypasses Python kernel call counters; cached autotune; fused experts; token shape/replay rows; variable expert load.
nodes.hypothesis: A faster component can improve serving only if it is actually dispatched on the critical path and does not lose KV capacity.
nodes.next_test: Record library versions and build config; capture kernel names outside and inside replay; qualify microbench before expensive paired serving run.
nodes.remaining_gap: Internal Generic/GenPhase dispatch is in external libraries and not established by SGLang flags. Planned: capture-time variant manifest plus replay-key linkage; do not add Python per-kernel counters and call them runtime counts.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Expert imbalance versus rebalance overhead
nodes.behavior: Expert placement responds to measured expert load; imbalance and rebalance costs can oppose each other.
conditions: EPLB-compatible MoE backend and correctness fixes.
confounders: Draft expert exclusions; redundant expert memory; synchronous moves; hot expert distribution changes with workload.
nodes.hypothesis: Better balance may shorten wide-EP decode steps, but moving weights can cause latency spikes.
nodes.next_test: Compare fixed placement vs EPLB with accuracy and capture smoke first; profile worst-rank MoE duration and rebalance periods.
nodes.remaining_gap: Need bounded per-layer/rank imbalance summary and rebalance wall/exposed time; existing histogram alone is not a speedup measurement.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Host memory and placement
nodes.behavior: Host table placement can free HBM while introducing host lookup/transfer cost and competing with HiCache for CPU memory.
conditions: DSv4.1 host Engram; NUMA topology and huge-page availability matter.
confounders: Table sharing scope per worker vs node; CPU binding actually applied; huge pages; host cache size; collective width.
nodes.hypothesis: More HBM may improve concurrency, but host access can worsen TPOT; increasing host cache can cause host OOM.
nodes.next_test: Record actual CPU affinity, per-node page placement, per-layer huge-page coverage and host budget before workload. Keep staging/checksum I/O outside comparison windows; compare fixed shapes and cache state before changing layout or binding.
nodes.remaining_gap: Existing per-layer startup logs report layout, resident MiB, huge-page MiB and collapse errors. They do not measure exposed lookup time or prove effective CPU/NUMA placement; collect OS placement and competing file-I/O evidence.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: KV transfer versus waiting to start transfer
nodes.behavior: Destination allocation, transfer initiation, wire movement and completion observation are separate; a transfer queue does not uniquely indicate poor bandwidth.
conditions: PD backend supports relevant metrics; distinguish transfer engine from cache storage backend.
confounders: Rank mappings; NIC/fabric; current forward/poll interval; source readiness; completion aggregation; host receive.
nodes.hypothesis: Faster transfer helps only when transfer lies on the exposed handoff path; a growing queue may instead reflect delayed polling or unavailable source.
nodes.next_test: Correlate allocation, bootstrap, transfer size/latency and scheduler stage time; verify NIC placement and fabric outside SGLang.
nodes.remaining_gap: No per-request wire-vs-poll critical-path decomposition; completed-transfer metrics omit currently stuck transfers.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Explicit decode interval defers prefill before budget checks
nodes.behavior: After an extend batch, the configured interval is armed. Each subsequent scheduling encounter decrements it and skips prefill admission while it remains active. Under attention DP the extend flag is synchronized across ranks.
conditions: Normal scheduler path; DLLM branch bypasses this gate. Event requires tuning_observation_interval > 0.
confounders: A deferral can occur without waiting work; continuing chunks are separate from waiting_queue. Other ranks can arm the shared cadence. Gate encounters are not completed decode forwards or elapsed wait. Downstream capacity checks are not reached in deferred passes.
nodes.hypothesis: With queued or continuing prefill work, a long decode interval can reduce prefill service even with free KV and no token-budget encounter. Reducing it may increase logical throughput while worsening decode ITL.
nodes.next_test: At fixed concurrency, topology, cache warmup and budgets, compare interval24 versus a lower value only after sustained queued-work deferrals are observed. Compare prefill service, total/output throughput, TTFT and p10 decode speed; reverse the change if the workload tradeoff is unfavorable.
nodes.remaining_gap: No exposed wall-time or oldest eligible request age is attributed to this gate. Queue presence does not prove all queued requests are otherwise eligible.
nodes.evidence: Source-audited during GB200 Phase3 baseline setup; production-method enabled/disabled CPU behavior tested. Runtime causal benefit unmeasured.

nodes.name: prefill.decode_interval
nodes.availability: tuning_observation_interval > 0; event-driven window
nodes.interpretation: One true interval-gate return, remaining value after decrement. waiting_requests is local queue length and chunk_pending is 0/1. Repeated encounters are not unique requests or blocked time.

nodes.name: engram host table backing receipt
nodes.availability: Existing INFO once after dirty host-table load; WARNING when no huge pages, collapse errno logged on failure.
nodes.interpretation: Per-layer/rank layout, resident and huge-page MiB; unequal coverage is a possible translation/placement confounder, not a measured slowdown. Concurrent checkpoint I/O can compete with page-cache reclamation.

nodes.title: Lazy decoder-tail graphs inside prefill
nodes.behavior: Bounded decoder replay tails can use row-bucket graphs during eager prefill; first use captures and subsequent compatible shapes replay. Whole-prefill graph disablement does not disable this mechanism.
conditions: CUDA; tail_writes_source_kv; MAX_ROWS>0; graph-pool borrowing off; full-chunk workspace warm gate; compatible row bucket, MoE bound, replay and DP state. MIN_PREFILL_TOKENS controls breaking a tail out of a prefill graph, not the eager-prefill cap.
confounders: Cold lazy captures consume time and memory; whole-forward prefill_none can coexist with tail-layer replay. Capture logs emit only on TP rank0 and do not count subsequent replay or fallback.
nodes.hypothesis: Tail graph replay may reduce host launch overhead after capture; disabling it may reduce cold cost but regress steady-state service.
nodes.next_test: Separate capture-active windows from warmed service. Only test MAX_ROWS after establishing tail coverage and relevant CPU/GPU cost; hold model, request shape and pool capacities controlled.
nodes.remaining_gap: No fixed-cardinality replay/capture/fallback counter by row bucket and eligibility reason; existing log reports rank0 capture totals only.
nodes.evidence: Source audit plus baseline-r1 warmup capture receipts on 2026-10-22.

nodes.name: Decoder tail graph capture receipt
nodes.availability: Existing INFO emitted by TP rank0 for each newly captured graph.
nodes.interpretation: Rows, segments, per-capture/cumulative wall seconds and device allocation delta. Does not count replay/fallback; does not establish every rank has identical memory cost.
